label.sw: I. Kubaini ngeli — orodha ya maneno

body.sw: Katika Kiswahili na Kiingereza hakuna jinsia — nyumba ni nyumba, kitabu ni kitabu, hakuna tofauti yoyote ya kisarufi. Kivumishi 'kubwa' haibadiliki. Katika Kihispania na Kifaransa kuna jinsia mbili — ya kiume na ya kike. Katika Kirusi na Kijerumani kuna jinsia tatu. Angalia sentensi zilizoingizwa na msemaji. Je, kivumishi kinabadilika kulingana na nomino?
body.en: In Swahili and English there is no gender — a house is just a house, a book is just a book, no grammatical difference. The adjective 'big' never changes. In Spanish and French there are two genders. In Russian and German there are three genders. Look at the phrases entered by the speaker. Does the adjective change depending on the noun?

sw: Haibadiliki — hakuna jinsia
Inabadilika → jinsia ngapi? zipi? jinsi ya kujua jinsia ya nomino — kwa mwisho wa neno, kwa maana, au lazima kukumbuka?
en: Changes → how many genders? what are they? how to determine gender — by ending, by meaning, or must be memorized?

if_yes.sw: Tunga mfano mmoja wa nomino ya kila jinsia na utoe tafsiri kwa Kiswahili na Kiingereza.
if_yes.en: Give one example noun for each gender and provide its translation in Swahili and English.

body.sw: Katika lugha za Kibantu — Kiswahili, Kikurya, na nyingine nyingi — nomino zimegawanywa katika ngeli, si jinsia. Ngeli zinaweza kuwa nyingi — katika Kiswahili kuna karibu 15. Kila ngeli ina kiambishi chake. Kwa mfano: mtu — watu (m-/wa-), kitabu — vitabu (ki-/vi-), mti — miti (m-/mi-). Na kivumishi na kitenzi vinabadilika kulingana na ngeli. Angalia sentensi za msemaji. Je, kuna ngeli kama hizo katika lugha yako?
body.en: In Bantu languages — Swahili, Kikurya, and many others — nouns are divided into classes, not genders. There can be many classes — Swahili has about 15. Each class has its own prefix. For example: mtu — watu (m-/wa-), kitabu — vitabu (ki-/vi-), mti — miti (m-/mi-). Both adjectives and verbs change according to class. Look at the speaker's phrases. Are there such classes in your language?

sw: Hakuna ngeli
Ndiyo → ngeli ngapi? viambishi gani vya umoja na wingi? tunga jedwali la ngeli na mifano na tafsiri
en: Yes → how many classes? what are the singular and plural prefixes? write a table of classes with examples and translations

body.sw: Angalia sentensi za msemaji — jinsi gani wingi huundwa katika lugha yako? Je, kuna nomino ambazo hazina wingi (kama maji, maziwa, chakula katika lugha nyingi)? Je, kuna nomino ambazo zipo katika wingi tu?
body.en: Look at the speaker's phrases — how is the plural formed in your language? Are there nouns with no plural (like water, milk, food in many languages)? Are there nouns that exist only in plural?

body.sw: Angalia sentensi ambapo John anamwona Anna na John anaona nyumba. Je, kuna tofauti katika umbo la neno 'Anna' na 'nyumba' katika sentensi hizi?
body.en: Look at the phrases where John sees Anna and John sees a house. Is there a difference in the form of the word 'Anna' and 'house' in these sentences?

body.sw: Angalia sentensi ambapo nomino moja ipo katika nafasi tofauti — mtendaji, mtendewa, umiliki, baada ya kihusishi. Je, umbo la nomino linabadilika? Katika Kiswahili John daima ni John. Katika Kirusi — Чача / Чачу / Чаче / о Чаче — inabadilika kila wakati.
body.en: Look at the phrases where the same noun appears in different roles — subject, object, possession, after a preposition. Does the form of the noun change? In Swahili John is always John. In Russian — Чача / Чачу / Чаче / о Чаче — it changes every time.

sw: Haibadiliki — hakuna hali
Inabadilika → hali ngapi? tunga jedwali na mifano na tafsiri
en: Changes → how many cases? write a table with examples and translations

body.sw: Angalia sentensi ambapo John anaona nyumba mara ya kwanza na John anaingia nyumba ile ile. Je, kuna tofauti katika lugha yako kati ya 'nyumba fulani' na 'nyumba ile ile tunayoijua'? Katika Kiingereza: a house / the house. Katika Kiswahili na Kirusi hakuna viwakilishi vya utambuzi — utambuzi unaonyeshwa kwa muktadha.
body.en: Look at the phrases where John sees a house for the first time and John enters that same house. Is there a difference in your language between 'some house' and 'that same house we already know'? In English: a house / the house. In Swahili and Russian there are no articles — definiteness is shown by context.

sw: Hakuna viwakilishi — utambuzi unaonyeshwa kwa muktadha
Kuna viwakilishi → vipi? vinabadilika vipi kulingana na jinsia/ngeli?
Utambuzi unaonyeshwa kwa njia nyingine → eleza na toa mifano
en: No articles — definiteness shown by context
There are articles → what are they? how do they change by gender/class?
Definiteness expressed another way → describe and give examples

body.sw: Kulingana na maudhui yote yaliyoingizwa — sentensi za wasemaji na majibu ya maswali hapo juu — tunga kitabu cha sarufi kuhusu nomino katika lugha yako.
body.en: Based on all content provided — speakers' phrases and answers to the questions above — write a grammar reference on nouns in your language.

body.sw: Kabla ya wasemaji kuanza kuingiza msamiati, tunahitaji kuelewa muundo wa kitenzi katika lugha yako. Tunakuomba utafsiri na utamke kitenzi 'kula' katika maumbo yote iwezekanavyo. Kama mfumo huo haupo katika lugha yako — acha wazi tu. Usibuni mfumo kama haupo. Kama huna uhakika — acha wazi na andika maoni.
body.en: Before speakers start entering vocabulary, we need to understand the structure of the verb in your language. Please translate and record the verb 'to eat' in all possible forms. If a particular form does not exist in your language — leave it blank. Do not invent a form if it does not exist. If you are not sure — leave it blank and write a comment.

present_simple.sw: Wakati wa sasa wa kawaida — tendo ambalo hutokea kwa kawaida, mara kwa mara, kama ukweli. Si sasa hivi bali kwa ujumla. Mfano: ninakula kila siku
present_simple.en: Present simple — action that happens regularly, as a general fact. Not right now but in general. Example: I eat every day

present_continuous.sw: Wakati wa sasa unaoendelea — tendo ambalo linatokea sasa hivi, dakika hii, katika mchakato. Mfano: ninakula sasa hivi (katika mchakato)
present_continuous.en: Present continuous — action happening right now, at this very moment, in progress. Example: I am eating right now (in progress)

present_perfect.sw: Wakati wa sasa uliokamilika — tendo ambalo limekwisha kumalizika na matokeo yake yanaonekana sasa. Mfano: nimekwisha kula (nimeshiba sasa)
present_perfect.en: Present perfect — action already finished, result visible now. Example: I have already eaten (I am full now)

present_perfect_continuous.sw: Wakati wa sasa uliokamilika unaoendelea — tendo ambalo lilianza zamani, liliendelea kwa muda mrefu na bado linaendelea. Mfano: nimekuwa nikila kwa muda mrefu
present_perfect_continuous.en: Present perfect continuous — action that started in the past, continued for a long time and is still ongoing. Example: I have been eating for a long time

past_simple.sw: Wakati wa kale — tendo ambalo lilitokea zamani na limekwisha. Mfano: nilikula (ukweli wa zamani)
past_simple.en: Past simple — action that happened in the past and is finished. Example: I ate (fact in the past)

past_continuous.sw: Wakati wa kale unaoendelea — tendo ambalo lilikuwa katika mchakato wakati fulani zamani. Mfano: nilikuwa nikila (John alipofika)
past_continuous.en: Past continuous — action that was in progress at a specific moment in the past. Example: I was eating (when John arrived)

past_perfect.sw: Wakati wa kale uliokamilika — tendo ambalo lilikwisha kumalizika kabla ya wakati mwingine zamani. Mfano: nilikuwa nimekwisha kula (John alipofika)
past_perfect.en: Past perfect — action that was completed before another moment in the past. Example: I had already eaten (by the time John arrived)

past_perfect_continuous.sw: Wakati wa kale uliokamilika unaoendelea — tendo ambalo lilikuwa likiendelea kwa muda mrefu hadi wakati fulani zamani. Mfano: nilikuwa nikila kwa muda mrefu (John alipofika)
past_perfect_continuous.en: Past perfect continuous — action that had been continuing for a long time up to a moment in the past. Example: I had been eating for a long time (when John arrived)

future_simple.sw: Wakati wa kesho — tendo ambalo litatokea siku zijazo. Mfano: nitakula (kesho)
future_simple.en: Future simple — action that will happen in the future. Example: I will eat (tomorrow)

future_continuous.sw: Wakati wa kesho unaoendelea — tendo ambalo litakuwa katika mchakato wakati fulani siku zijazo. Mfano: nitakuwa nikila (saa hiyo kesho)
future_continuous.en: Future continuous — action that will be in progress at a specific moment in the future. Example: I will be eating (at that time tomorrow)

future_perfect.sw: Wakati wa kesho uliokamilika — tendo ambalo litakuwa limekwisha kumalizika kabla ya wakati fulani siku zijazo. Mfano: nitakuwa nimekwisha kula (Anna atakapofika)
future_perfect.en: Future perfect — action that will have been completed before a specific moment in the future. Example: I will have already eaten (by the time Anna arrives)

future_perfect_continuous.sw: Wakati wa kesho uliokamilika unaoendelea — tendo ambalo litakuwa limekuwa likiendelea kwa muda mrefu hadi wakati fulani siku zijazo.
future_perfect_continuous.en: Future perfect continuous — action that will have been continuing for a long time up to a moment in the future.

conditional.sw: Masharti — tendo ambalo lingetokea kama sharti lingetimizwa. Mfano: ningekula (kama ningekuwa na njaa)
conditional.en: Conditional — action that would happen if a condition were met. Example: I would eat (if I were hungry)

conditional_perfect.sw: Masharti uliokamilika — tendo ambalo lingelikuwa limekwisha kutokea kama sharti lingelikuwa limetimizwa.
conditional_perfect.en: Conditional perfect — action that would have been completed if a condition had been met.

forms_to_fill.note_sw: Kama mfumo haupo katika lugha yako — acha wazi. Usibuni.
forms_to_fill.note_en: If a form does not exist in your language — leave blank. Do not invent.

body.sw: Kulingana na vitenzi vyote vilivyoingizwa — je, kuna maumbo tofauti ya unyambulishaji? Kwa mfano katika Kihispania kuna vitenzi vya -AR, -ER, -IR — kila kikundi kina mfumo wake tofauti. Katika Kiswahili mfumo ni sawa kwa vitenzi vyote — tofauti ni katika mzizi tu. Je, katika lugha yako kuna aina tofauti za unyambulishaji?
body.en: Looking at all the verbs entered — are there different conjugation patterns? For example in Spanish there are -AR, -ER, -IR verbs — each group has its own pattern. In Swahili the pattern is the same for all verbs — the difference is only in the root. Are there different conjugation types in your language?

sw: Hapana — mfumo mmoja kwa vitenzi vyote
Ndiyo — kuna aina tofauti → ngapi? vipi zinavyotofautiana? jinsi ya kujua kikundi cha kitenzi?
en: No — one pattern for all verbs
Yes — there are different types → how many? how do they differ? how to determine which group a verb belongs to?

body.sw: Angalia jedwali la kitenzi 'kula' ulilolijaza. Ni nyakati zipi zilizopo katika lugha yako? Ni zipi ambazo hazipo? Kama kuna nyakati ambazo hazilingani na mifano tuliyotoa — zieleze na utoe mifano.
body.en: Look at the table of the verb 'to eat' you filled in. Which tenses exist in your language? Which ones don't exist? If there are tenses that don't match the examples we provided — describe them and give examples.

sw: Orodha ya nyakati zilizopo
Orodha ya nyakati ambazo hazipo
Nyakati za ziada ambazo hazikuwa katika orodha yetu — eleza na toa mifano
en: Additional tenses not in our list — describe and give examples

body.sw: Katika Kirusi kuna tofauti kati ya 'kufanya' (mchakato, haujamalizika) na 'kukamilisha' (umalizika). Kwa mfano: 'nilikula' (nilikuwa nikila, sijamalizia) na 'nilikwisha kula' (nimefanya, nimekwisha). Je, kuna tofauti kama hiyo katika lugha yako?
body.en: In Russian there is a difference between 'to do' (process, not completed) and 'to complete' (finished). For example: 'I was eating' (process) and 'I finished eating' (completed). Is there such a distinction in your language?

sw: Hapana — hakuna tofauti kama hiyo
Ndiyo → eleza jinsi inavyofanya kazi na toa mifano
en: Yes → describe how it works and give examples

body.sw: Angalia sentensi za ukanushi katika jedwali lako. Jinsi gani ukanushi huundwa katika lugha yako? Je, umbo la kitenzi hubadilika wakati wa ukanushi? Je, kuna ukanushi mara mbili (kama Kirusi — 'sijawahi kwenda')?
body.en: Look at the negative sentences in your table. How is negation formed in your language? Does the verb form change in negation? Is there double negation (like Russian — 'I have never gone')?

sw: Kwa kiambishi awali
Kwa neno tofauti kabla ya kitenzi

Kuna ukanushi mara mbili → toa mifano
en: By a separate word before the verb

body.sw: Kulingana na maudhui yote yaliyoingizwa — jedwali la kitenzi 'kula', sentensi za wasemaji na majibu ya maswali hapo juu — tunga kitabu cha sarufi kuhusu kitenzi katika lugha yako.
body.en: Based on all content provided — the table of 'to eat', speakers' sentences and answers to the questions above — write a grammar reference on verbs in your language.

body.sw: Katika Kiswahili 'watu wawili' lakini 'vitabu viwili' — neno 'wawili/viwili' linabadilika kulingana na ngeli. Katika Kiingereza 'two' haibadiliki kamwe. Katika lugha yako — nambari inabadilika kulingana na kitu au daima ni sawa?

body.sw: Katika baadhi ya lugha nambari 1 na 2 zina maumbo maalum — zinapatana na nomino tofauti na nambari nyingine. Kwa mfano katika Kirusi nambari 1 na 2 zinabadilika kulingana na jinsia. Katika lugha yako — nambari 1 na 2 zina maalum au zinafanya kazi kama nyingine zote?
body.en: In some languages numbers 1 and 2 have special forms — they agree with nouns differently from other numbers. In Russian numbers 1 and 2 change by gender. In your language — do numbers 1 and 2 have special forms or work like all other numbers?
